name: Digital cash
title: Why DigiCash failed, and when digital cash became viable
question: Why did DigiCash fail, and when did digital cash become viable?
answer: DigiCash (1989) built private, cryptographic electronic cash and filed for bankruptcy in 1998 after few banks adopted it. Its design needed a trusted issuer that banks would not become. Bitcoin (2009) removed the issuer with proof-of-work consensus, a protocol invention nobody could have scheduled; dollar stablecoins such as USDC (2018) later combined the two ideas.
verdict_reason: Decentralised consensus (2009) removed the need for an issuing bank.

constraint.name: Issuer-free consensus
constraint.detail: Digital cash needed someone to prevent double-spending; until 2009 that had to be a bank.
